title: Baby Steps
genre: Physics-based walking simulator / 'rage' traversal game (QWOP / Getting Over It lineage) with narrative comedy
release_date: 2025-09-23 (Windows/Steam and PS5) [CONFIRMED – Devolver/Indigo Pearl press release; moved from 2025-09-08 to avoid Hollow Knight: Silksong]
early_access_date: n/a (free Steam demo, app 2460140; PS Plus Premium 1-hour trial after launch)
developer: Gabe Cuzzillo, Maxi Boch and Bennett Foddy
team_size: 3 core developers [CONFIRMED – Wikipedia / Devolver / Foddy's site]. Cuzzillo also voices the protagonist Nate; additional audio/voice contributors not counted.
country: USA (New York; the team worked from a shared office at the NYU Game Center)
developer_background: Veteran trio. Bennett Foddy made QWOP (2008) and Getting Over It with Bennett Foddy (2017), a streamer phenomenon. Cuzzillo (Foddy's former NYU student) made Ape Out (Devolver, 2019) with Foddy and Boch (Boch was Foddy's NYU Game Center colleague). They started Baby Steps right after Ape Out; Cuzzillo pitched a more refined QWOP. Early prototypes included a golf game, a twin-stick shooter, a competitive SimCity and a Populous-style god game.
platforms_and_store_links: Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1281040/Baby_Steps/ ; Steam demo (app 2460140): https://steamcharts.com/app/2460140 ; PS5 (PlayStation Store; PS Plus Premium trial) ; Devolver page: https://www.devolverdigital.com/games/baby-steps
business_model: Premium $19.99 (PC and PS5); 10% PS Plus member discount and 1-hour PS Plus Premium trial at launch; no DLC or IAP found.
units_or_downloads: No official sales figure found (Devolver's 2025 operating review only says Baby Steps 'performed well' with Metacritic 76 and 90% positive Steam reviews) [CONFIRMED – Devolver 2025 report via financialfilings.com]. Steam estimates: ~51.7k copies as of 2026-07-22 [ESTIMATE – Raijin]; 96,455 units [ESTIMATE – VG Insights via SteamPulse, undated]; ~77k [ESTIMATE – Boxleiter: 2,579 reviews × 30]. PS5 sales: no data.
peak_concurrent_players: 1,032 all-time peak on 2025-09-25 [ESTIMATE – Steambase; SteamCharts lists 1,019]. Fell to ~316 monthly peak by Mar 2026 and ~49–115 by Jul 2026 [ESTIMATE – SteamCharts/Steambase]. Note: the game's reach was mostly via streams/videos, not Steam concurrents.
steam_reviews: ~2,579 reviews, 90% positive ('Very Positive'), ~Jul 2026 [ESTIMATE – Raijin]; 2,276 reviews in Apr 2026 [Steambase]; 2,287 / 91% [SteamPulse].
implied_review_multiplier: n/a (no confirmed unit figure). Trackers imply ~20 (Raijin 51.7k ÷ 2,572) to ~42 (VGI 96k ÷ 2,287). I used 30 (single-player enthusiast game with an engaged community).
gross_revenue: Steam ≈ $1.0–1.3M lifetime to ~Jul 2026 [ESTIMATE – Boxleiter: ~77k × $19.99 × 0.75 ≈ $1.16M; VG Insights $1.3M; Raijin $619.7k (medium confidence)]. PS5 revenue: no data.
net_revenue: Steam ≈ $0.65–0.85M [ESTIMATE – $1.0–1.3M × 0.70 (gross < $10M) × 0.93], before the Devolver / developer split (not disclosed). PS5: no data.
production_cost: No disclosed figure. ≈ $0.8–1.3M [ESTIMATE – 3 people × ~70 months (late 2019 – Sep 2025) × ~$4k–$6k/month (US lean indie); likely part-time for Foddy, who also teaches at NYU], plus Devolver marketing (Devolver Direct 2023 reveal, Summer Game Fest / State of Play trailers).
development_time: ~6 years: Foddy says he worked on it 'from late 2019 to 2025' [CONFIRMED – foddy.net, Feb 2026]; Engadget dates the first prototyping to ~March 2019. Revealed June 2023 (Devolver Direct).
why_popular: Pedigree and premise: the next game from the makers of QWOP, Getting Over It and Ape Out. You control each of Nate's legs manually (a lazy, onesie-clad 'failson') up a huge open mountain where any misstep sends you tumbling back down. It is a pure streamer and clip machine: dramatic falls, slapstick physics, awkward-funny dialogue and Getting Over It-style rage. Its emotional appeal is perseverance, with a surprisingly heartfelt story under the absurd humour. Critically well received (Metacritic 76, 90% positive on Steam) but niche in sales; its cultural reach (streams, clips) far exceeded its Steam concurrents.
marketing_channels: Devolver Direct (June 2023 reveal) and Devolver's comedic marketing; Sony State of Play (June 2025); free Steam demo; Twitch/YouTube streamers and clip culture built on Foddy's name (no viewership data found); press features/interviews (Engadget, Kill Screen, podcasts); PS Plus Premium trial and member discount; release moved to avoid Silksong.
engine: no data (not named in any source found; Ape Out, the trio's previous game, is documented as Unity – not confirmed for Baby Steps)
art_style: Stylised 3D with a soft, painterly/low-detail open mountain landscape; a doughy, physically simulated protagonist in a grey onesie; comedic character dialogue
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write procedural leg/IK control code, ragdoll/active-ragdoll scaffolding, save/checkpoint systems and camera; generate terrain props and textures (Meshy/Tripo, Scenario), placeholder dialogue, SFX (ElevenLabs) and music (Suno). | AI cannot: deliver the hard part, the physics 'feel' of stepping (years of iteration even for veterans), hand-crafted level/terrain design that rewards and punishes precisely, comedic writing and voice timing, and Foddy's brand and streamer pull. The 'feel'/polish bar puts it at 3; a smaller 'similar in spirit' rage-climber with one mechanic is closer to 4. | Toolset: Claude Code + Unity (PhysX, Animation Rigging) or Godot 4 (Jolt); Meshy/Tripo for 3D; Scenario/Midjourney for textures; ElevenLabs for SFX/voice; Suno music; Steamworks.NET/GodotSteam.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 1–2 months, $200–$600 for a one-mechanic physics rage-climber prototype (Claude Pro/Max, 3D gen $20–$60/mo, Steam Direct $100). Excludes the developer's own living costs.
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 6–12 months, $3,000–$12,000 (subscriptions, freelance character/animation and voice polish, playtests, trailer, streamer key outreach). Excludes living costs. A full Baby Steps-scale open mountain with narrative is beyond a solo dev in this time.

data_conflicts: Units: Raijin ~51.7k (Jul 2026) vs VG Insights 96,455 (undated) vs my Boxleiter ~77k (×30); revenue $620k (Raijin) vs $1.3M (VGI). I report a range. Peak CCU: 1,032 (Steambase, 2025-09-25) vs 1,019 (SteamCharts). Dev start: Engadget ~Mar 2019 prototyping vs Foddy 'late 2019'. Release date: some localised articles say 2025-09-08 (the original date); the confirmed date is 2025-09-23. Reception: one outlet described launch reception as mixed, while Steam is 90% positive and Metacritic 76.
notes: Cautionary benchmark: famous creators + a strong streamer hook + a top publisher still produced only ~1k peak CCU and an estimated ~$1M on Steam at $19.99. 'Streamer-viral' (people watching) is not the same as 'buyer-viral' (people buying and playing together). Rage/precision games are watched more than bought. Compare How to Fish / co-op friendslop, which converts viewers into multi-pack buyers at a low price. The 6-year dev time on a single physics mechanic shows how expensive feel-driven games are. A solo+AI dev should scope a rage-climber to one mechanic and a short, dense course (as Getting Over It did) rather than an open world.
